guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 for applications that act for individual users. The default read scope gives read access to the authorizing user's account and is the least-privilege match for reading issue titles. Pagination is documented with first/after cursors and pageInfo. Setup requires registering an OAuth2 application with redirect URIs and exchanging the code for tokens. Access tokens last 24 hours and are refreshed with refresh tokens. Distribution to other customer organizations is not resolved from the supplied snapshots.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Call the GraphQL endpoint with the access token and request the first 10 issues with id, title and pageInfo. The default order is createdAt. Confirm the response contains issue titles under data.issues.nodes and pageInfo.hasNextPage.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns data.issues.nodes with title values and a pageInfo object including hasNextPage and endCursor. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: # Pagination All list responses from queries return paginated results. We implement Relay style cursor-based pagination model with `first`/`after` and `last`/`before` pagination arguments. For example, this is how to query
} ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues { issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: returned by the code exchange step for the connected test user
Titles are read from data.issues.nodes[].title

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using the returned cursor
steps.detail: Pass the pageInfo.endCursor value from the first response as the after argument, preserving first: 10. Repeat while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true. Stop when hasNextPage is false; a single extra page is not a full listing. Repeat the after-cursor request with the latest pageInfo.endCursor until the response reports hasNextPage false. Use the same page size and query shape each time.
steps.doneWhen: The second request returns further issue titles and the listing ends when pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. pageInfo.hasNextPage is false in the most recent response, so all issue titles have been read. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues($after: String) { issues(first: 10, after: $after) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"after":"<END_CURSOR>"}}'

fields: END_CURSOR: pageInfo.endCursor from the prior response in the same query
